title: Is Japan’s Repatriation Wave Starting?
text:
Is Japan’s Repatriation Wave Starting?

Udith Sikand

Gavekal Research | 6 Nov 2026

It has long been one of the big questions hanging over global financial markets: at what point will Japanese portfolio investors decide the relative rewards of holding US$5trn in overseas assets no longer outweigh the risks, and begin to repatriate capital in earnest. Every so often, the expectation of increased repatriation flows is enough to trigger a nasty bout of global volatility, as it did in the summer of 2024.Since then, the rise in Japanese government bond yields has quietly changed the calculus for Japanese investors. So far it is more a trickle than a flood, but over the 12 months to September, Japanese investors repatriated a net ¥5.5trn of foreign portfolio assets. Now, the latest evolution of the Bank of Japan’s stance, apparent at its late-October policy meeting, may lend additional momentum to the incipient flow. If so, it could create a structural bid for the yen, one of the world’s most undervalued currencies.
